launches.name: AntiSniperHook
launches.summary: Hamster Hour — fixed-supply launch token with a decaying anti-sniper hook on Ethereum mainnet.
launches.request:
Hamster Hour — fixed-supply launch token with a decaying anti-sniper
hook on Ethereum mainnet. No game, no betting, no lottery: this launch
is the token and its hook only.

Contracts:

1. HamsterHourToken (ERC-20)
   name "Hamster Hour", symbol HAMSTER, 18 decimals.
   Supply 1,000,000,000 minted once to msg.sender in the constructor.
   No owner, no mint, no burn, no pause, no transfer fee, no blacklist,
   no upgrade path. This token has NO fee on transfer of any kind: a
   plain transfer always moves the full amount.

2. AntiSniperHook (Uniswap v4 hook)
   Attached to the Hamster Hour v4 pool. The pool pairs HAMSTER with
   IMD (0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7, 18 decimals, the
   IMD token on Ethereum mainnet). IMD is the quote asset.

   On every buy the hook takes a fee from the input amount and sends it
   to FEE_RECIPIENT. The fee rate decays linearly from START_BPS to
   FLOOR_BPS over DECAY_SECONDS, then stays at FLOOR_BPS forever:

     elapsed = block.timestamp - poolInitialisedAt
     if elapsed >= DECAY_SECONDS:
         feeBps = FLOOR_BPS
     else:
         feeBps = FLOOR_BPS
                + (START_BPS - FLOOR_BPS) * (DECAY_SECONDS - elapsed)
                  / DECAY_SECONDS

   Constants fixed in DeploymentConfig as immutable constructor
   arguments:
     START_BPS     = 3000   (30% at launch)
     FLOOR_BPS     = 500    (5% permanent floor, never removed)
     DECAY_SECONDS = 600    (10 minutes; 25 percentage points per minute)
     FEE_RECIPIENT = 0xbb85c1b7540d9e7b56f7a595fc1ff7dd07cb0823
                     as this literal; the constructor reverts if it is
                     the zero address

   Buys only. The fee applies only when the swap input is IMD (a buy).
   When the input is Hamster Hour (a sell), feeBps is 0
   unconditionally: selling must always work and is never taxed. A sell
   must succeed at any time, including t=0, with zero fee.

   The hook is immutable: START_BPS, FLOOR_BPS, DECAY_SECONDS,
   FEE_RECIPIENT and poolInitialisedAt are written once in the
   constructor and can never be changed. No owner, no setter, no pause,
   no rescue, no sweep. The floor never expires and the fee never
   reaches zero. The fee recipient has no function to call and no power
   over the pool.

3. The hook must never be able to block a sell, block a transfer,
   revert a buy, or change its own parameters. It holds no funds
   between transactions: the fee is transferred to FEE_RECIPIENT inside
   the swap.

Rules: no owner, no pause, no proxy on any contract. Static constructor
arguments. All parameters fixed in DeploymentConfig.

Tests must pass: forge test, and forge test --fork-url on mainnet with
a real v4 HAMSTER/IMD pool, proving:
- the fee at t=0 is exactly 3000 bps
- the fee at t=300s is exactly 1750 bps
- the fee at t=599s is above FLOOR_BPS
- the fee at t>=600s is exactly 500 bps and never changes again
- the fee never returns to zero at any time
- a sell is never taxed at any time, including t=0 and after decay
- a plain ERC-20 transfer is never taxed
- the fee recipient receives exactly the fee amount on a taxed buy

Chain: Ethereum mainnet. Pair with IMD. Source on GitHub.

launches.request:
CROWN - a per-ticker crown registry and Uniswap v4 fee hook. Build the full system, deploy it on Robinhood Chain (chainId 4663), and deliver a working end-to-end demo.

CONCEPT: One canonical token per ticker - the king. A registry contract maps ticker -> {kingToken, beneficiary, reignStartedAt}. A Uniswap v4 hook attached to participating pools skims a cut of every swap and pays it, inside the same transaction, to the current king`s beneficiary wallet (pay-at-source: fees must never be stored in the hook or pooled for claiming). Anyone can challenge the king with a bonded ETH stake-vote; if the challenger out-stakes the king within the window and quorum is met, the registry flips after a timelock and every subsequent swap pays the new king.

CONTRACT 1 - CrownRegistry:
- ticker is bytes32 = keccak256 of the uppercase symbol string.
- registerKing(ticker, token, beneficiary): the first registration for a ticker crowns that token.
- openChallenge(ticker, challengerToken) payable: bond 0.01 ETH; one live challenge per ticker; a king is challengeable only after a 7-day minimum reign; 3-day cooldown per ticker after a failed challenge.
- stake(challengeId, side) payable in ETH during a 72-hour window (side = king or challenger).
- finalize(challengeId) after the window plus a 24-hour timelock: the challenger wins iff challenger stake > king stake AND total staked >= 0.05 ETH quorum. On a flip, the registry points to the challenger token and its beneficiary. Losing side: 80% refundable to its stakers (pull pattern), 20% slashed - half of the slash pro-rata to winning-side stakers (pull), half to treasury 0xf19F11Dee16a341671E6Ed3e209b704C1Bbc3E57. Winning side`s stake is fully refundable (pull).
- Events: Crowned, ChallengeOpened, Staked, Dethroned, ChallengeFailed. Public per-ticker totals.
- No admin functions after deployment beyond the constructor`s parameter init; resolution is purely rule-based.

CONTRACT 2 - CrownHook (Uniswap v4; afterSwap and afterSwapReturnsDelta permissions):
- afterInitialize records poolId -> ticker; the deployer registers each pool`s ticker explicitly.
- On every swap: compute the cut (per-pool bps set at init, default 100, range 0-500) from the swap amount, read registry.king(ticker).beneficiary, take the cut as the hook`s delta and transfer it to the beneficiary within the same settlement. Maintain a public counter crownPaid[ticker][currency] (cumulative).
- The hook must never revert or block a swap: if the registry read or the transfer fails, the swap proceeds without the cut.

DEMO LAUNCH (this launch`s token): name "Crown Demo", symbol CRWN, paired with native ETH on Robinhood Chain, pool wearing CrownHook, registered as genesis king of ticker CRWN with beneficiary = the launch payer wallet. Additionally deploy a second, distinct plain ERC-20 with the same name and symbol CRWN (a deploy script is fine) as the standing challenger candidate, so a full dethrone (challenge, stake, finalize, recipient flip) can be executed end-to-end after launch.

SITE: the canonical ticker page - current king per ticker, crownPaid totals per ticker, live challenge state (window, both stakes, time remaining), stake and challenge actions wired to the contracts, and a plain-English how-it-works section.

TESTS (Foundry, in the repo): registry and challenge math unit tests (bond, quorum, slash split exact to the wei) and a Uniswap v4 integration test executing buy -> challenge -> stake -> finalize -> buy, asserting the fee recipient changed and crownPaid matches the transfers. Contracts must compile with the repo`s pinned settings and be Sourcify-verifiable; record the compiler settings in the README.

launches.request:
Launch DEF (name "DEF", symbol "DEF") on a DEF/ETH Uniswap v4 pool whose hook is a reflection fee hook.
The hook has one job: keep 2.25% of the DEF side of every swap and hand it, on request, to one address called the sink.
It never takes ETH, never swaps, never touches liquidity, has no pause, no rate change, no blocklist, no upgrade.

FEE RULE (constant, 225 bps, immutable)
- Buy (ETH in, DEF out): in afterSwap, fee = 2.25% of the DEF the swap produced. Mint the fee to the hook as a
  PoolManager claim (ERC-6909) on the DEF currency and return it as the hook's int128 delta, so the swapper
  receives 97.75% and the hook keeps 2.25%.
- Sell (DEF in, ETH out): in beforeSwap, fee = 2.25% of the DEF specified. Mint it to the hook as a claim and
  return toBeforeSwapDelta(fee, 0) so only 97.75% enters the pool.
- Exact-output swaps revert with ExactOutputUnsupported(). Only exact-input is supported, in both directions.
- Emit ReflectionFee(address indexed swapper, bool buy, uint256 defAmount) on every fee.
- Nothing else is ever charged. The hook's ETH balance and ETH claim balance are always zero.

COLLECTION AND THE SINK
- sink() view returns address. setSink(address) is owner-only, refuses the zero address, emits
  SinkSet(address indexed sink), and may be called again later (the sink can be moved by the owner only).
- collected() view: the hook's DEF claim balance in the PoolManager, i.e. the fee waiting to be flushed.
- flush() callable by anyone: burns the hook's whole DEF claim and takes the DEF to sink inside
  poolManager.unlock, emits Flushed(address indexed sink, uint256 amount), reverts SinkNotSet() while sink is
  zero and NothingToFlush() when collected() is zero. Returns the amount.
- Fee-source face, so the sink can pull without a keeper calling flush first. These two functions must exist with
  these exact signatures and semantics:
  - function claimable(address account, address currency) external view returns (uint256): returns
    collected() when account == sink and currency == address(DEF), otherwise 0.
  - function claim(address currency, address to) external returns (uint256 amount): callable only by the sink
    (revert NotSink()), to must equal the sink, currency must be the DEF token (revert WrongCurrency());
    performs the same transfer as flush() and returns the amount.

POOL AND LAUNCH CONSTRAINTS
- The pool is DEF against native ETH (currency0 = address(0), currency1 = DEF), LP fee 0, tick spacing 60, this hook.
- beforeInitialize and beforeAddLiquidity accept only the launch (the factory / the hook itself), so the pool is
  the one launched and its liquidity is the launch liquidity; any later initialize with this hook reverts, and any
  later add-liquidity reverts LiquidityLocked(). Remove-liquidity and donate hooks are no-ops.
- Hook permissions: BEFORE_INITIALIZE, BEFORE_ADD_LIQUIDITY, BEFORE_SWAP, AFTER_SWAP, BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA,
  AFTER_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA. Nothing else.
- Views: poolKey() returns the PoolKey, poolId() returns bytes32, def() the token, owner(), FEE_BPS() = 225.
- Custom errors: NotPoolManager, NotOwner, LiquidityLocked, ExactOutputUnsupported, ZeroAddress,
  SinkNotSet, NothingToFlush, WrongCurrency, NotSink.

OWNER'S POWERS, EXHAUSTIVELY
setSink only. No withdrawal path exists except flush() / claim() to the sink. No admin can take DEF or ETH.

OUTSIDE SERVICES AND VALUES
None. No oracle, no price feed, no signer, no backend, no external contract beyond the Uniswap v4 PoolManager and
the DEF token. The only value set after launch is the sink address, by the owner, through setSink.

TESTS THE BUILD MUST INCLUDE
1. A buy of X ETH delivers 97.75% of the swap's DEF output to the buyer and collected() rises by 2.25% (within 1 wei).
2. A sell of Y DEF charges 2.25% of Y into the hook before the swap; the pool receives 97.75%.
3. An exact-output swap in either direction reverts ExactOutputUnsupported.
4. The hook's ETH balance and ETH claim balance stay zero after buys, sells and flushes.
5. flush() reverts SinkNotSet before setSink, moves exactly collected() to the sink after it, then reverts
   NothingToFlush.
6. claimable(sink, DEF) equals collected(); claimable(other, DEF) and claimable(sink, other) are 0;
   claim from a non-sink reverts NotSink; claim(DEF, sink) from the sink moves the amount and zeroes collected().
7. A non-owner calling setSink reverts NotOwner; setSink(address(0)) reverts ZeroAddress.
8. Adding liquidity after the launch reverts LiquidityLocked.

- vote(epoch, id, amount): epoch == currentEpoch(); burns amount, recorded per voter.
- A vote in the last hour extends the end to 10 min after it, max +24h.
- flag(epoch, id, note): KEEPER; note max 120 bytes.
- settle(epoch): anyone, after the end. Most burned wins (tie: earlier); runner-up recorded. Winner's burns under 0.01 ETH at the epoch TWAP: no winner (status 4).

OVERVIEW:
Token name: Perkshire IMDway
Token symbol: PERK
This launch is the hook and the token only; logo and website are a later job.
Perkshire IMDway ($PERK) is a value-investing parody token on Robinhood Chain, paired with IMD. Its Uniswap v4 hook is also its Retained Earnings Vault: every trade pays 1% in IMD to the hook. Half is burned as IMD (the buyback) and half stays as the "insurance float"; any holder can tender PERK to the float at book value at any time. Once a week the float buys one answer from the IMD oracle (the Chairman's weekly report): the vault is a paying customer of the swarm. Tendered PERK is burned. Book value per PERK, in IMD terms, rises only from the float, never from newly issued tokens; a tender leaves it unchanged. Book value starts at zero and, at realistic volume, stays far below market price; it only matters if price falls to it. No emissions, rebases, staking APY, admin keys or promised yield. Parody only: not affiliated with Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett or Charlie Munger; PERK is not a share or equity in any company.

CONTRACT: one hook that is also the vault, plus the standard PERK token. No owner, admin or upgrade. Pool: 89% of supply; 1% to the requester.
1. Binding: constructor takes $poolManager, $token (immutable perk), IMD 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127 (immutable imd) and $factory (immutable factory). beforeInitialize requires sender == factory, currencies exactly perk and imd, fee 12500, not dynamic, no pool bound yet; then binds that one pool. All other initializations revert. Do not hard-code tick spacing. Do not copy #1330's open binding. If $token cannot be passed, take perk from the pool the factory initializes: the currency that is not imd.
2. Float: reuse launch #1330's fee logic unchanged, RnnnFeeHook in https://github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-1330-launch-rnnn-bid-community-token at commit 7001624 (simulateSwap, return deltas, deferral, redeemPendingFees, same five permission bits) with the hook itself as fee recipient; only binding, burn, ask and tender are new. Every swap in the bound pool, both directions, exact-in and exact-out, takes 1% of the IMD the pool moves in that swap, as #1330 measures it, into the hook and emits FloatCollected. Half of each fee, rounded down, is added to burnOwed; the rest is added to totalFloat. This is on top of the pool's standard fee. Fees the PoolManager cannot pay out yet stay ERC-6909 claims held by the hook until anyone calls redeemPendingFees(). Both halves are counted when the fee is taken, paid or deferred; pendingFloat is the deferred part. Never count a fee twice. Burn: whenever the hook holds IMD (after a fee, a redeem, before a tender or an ask, or when anyone calls burn()), send min(burnOwed, balance) to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD, lower burnOwed, raise totalBurned, emit Burned; if IMD refuses the transfer, leave it owed and do not revert.

4. ask(): anyone, at most once every 7 days (the first at any time). Requires the hook's IMD less burnOwed to be at least 0.6 IMD. Approve exactly 0.5 IMD to the Intake 0xa43e6F75ee006411F79Ac1C84120606C2330DE82 and call request(bytes32 "oracle.request@oracle-1", BODY, callback (address(0), bytes4(0)), imd, 0.5 IMD); pay the caller 0.1 IMD; record lastAsk and totalAsked; emit Asked(requestId). launches.request: Audit and deploy Sherwood v2 on Robinhood Chain (4663) for $IMD, with no new token. Sherwood v2 (src/SherwoodV2.sol) is a Uniswap v4 hook running a leaderboard game in rolling 20-hour rounds on one native-ETH/$IMD pool: every buy scores points and pays 5% of its ETH into the round's pot. Moves are Buy, Steal, Robin Hood, Flip (Dice Protocol randomness) and Shield, with stacking charges. Each pot pays the top 3 40/20/10%, 8% to the King of the Hill (longest at #1), 10% buys back and burns $IMD through the existing ETH/$IMD 1% pool, 7% buys back and burns $PFWA (the host token) through its holder pool, and 5% rolls over. Prizes are claimed within 7 days; anything unclaimed goes into the live round's pot. A v4 hook needs its permission flags (0x20CC) in its address, and this launch takes no salt, so deploy ONE contract, src/SherwoodV2Launcher.sol:SherwoodV2Launcher, whose constructor finds the salt onchain and deploys the hook with CREATE2 (about 10M gas; rehearsed on a fork in test/SherwoodV2LauncherFork.t.sol). The hook is launcher.hook(). Constructor arguments, in order: poolManager 0x8366a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e40951, token ($IMD) 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127, host ($PFWA) 0xa934ba4f59070149d37a93f8a002af79bae35563, hostHolderMin 100000000000000000000000, dice 0xd8a0680e7699526b57140ed4eafdcc7219dc0a0c, diceProvider 0x8741b8a825644d9ef18faf2dab5e9b47b900f2b6, owner $owner, genesis 1791835200. Please keep the game rules and the split as they are; fix anything the audit finds. Focus: swap delta accounting and the two buyback swaps in unlockCallback, pot/prize/referral/claim/sweep accounting (ETH out can never exceed ETH in, and settlement can never revert), the flip lifecycle with Dice, the charge clocks, the King of the Hill reign tracking, and anything that could block swaps, settlement or claims. Our own notes for the audit are in README.md under Sherwood v2. This repository already carries the fixes from IMD launch 1355's audit of this code (ADAPTATION.md, revisions 1 and 2) and, in revision 3, the fix for the finding that parked that launch: settle now credits a final unknown spell to the round's final #1 (test_settleCreditsTheFinalUnknownSpellToTheFinalLeader). The runtime is 24,480 bytes, 96 under EIP-170.

launches.request:
Launch the BMC Illuminati Community token on Ethereum, paired with ETH on Uniswap v4.

Token
Name: BMC Illuminati
Symbol: BMC
Supply: 1,000,000,000 with 18 decimals, minted once.
Transfers: plain only — no fees, limits, pausing, or minting after launch. No owner powers.

Pool
Paired with ETH, opening at a 10 ETH market cap.
Standard trading fee: 1.25% of every trade — 1% claimable by the launcher, 0.25% to IMD.

Hook (attached to the pool this launch opens)

When the hook acts: on every swap.
Fee rule:
On buys: takes an additional 1% of the ETH side and sends it as ETH to 0x83027AD9d0D5374335086c539dADD1db983441B0.
On sells: burns 1% of the BMC tokens being sold (permanently reduces supply).
Where fees go: ETH fees go to the fixed community wallet above; sell burns go to the zero address.
Who can change it: nobody. All percentages and the recipient are immutable constructor arguments.
No owner, no pause, no other fees, does not block or alter swaps otherwise.
Utility note
Selling permanently removes tokens from supply. Over time this reduces circulating supply, which can support price if demand stays constant or grows. This is not a guaranteed price increase.

Split
10% to the swarm. The other 90% is the launcher’s: 88% into the pool, the rest to the launcher wallet.

Website
Build and publish a usable public site at bmcilluminati.sites.imd.fun.

The site shows:

Token name, symbol, contract, total supply + circulating supply (after burns)
Live Uniswap pool link
Clear explanation of the 1% sell burn and 1% buy fee to the community wallet
Buy/sell buttons and community links
Connected wallet can do

Connect and show BMC + ETH balances
Approve (exact amount) then buy/sell against the ETH pool
Claim the launcher’s 1% fee share if the connected wallet is the recipient
No admin actions
Include Foundry tests verifying the sell burn and the buy fee transfer.

Token name: Swarm Pepe
Token symbol: SPEPE

This launch implements Swarm Pepe (SPEPE), a standard ERC20 token with 1,000,000,000 supply and 18 decimals, minted once. 10% of supply (100 million SPEPE) is sent to 0xbda087645f96b8c64f15b08875332edb8bc19611; 80% seeds the Uniswap v4 pool with 1.25% fee and 60 tick spacing.

M1. Anti-snipe: during the first 10 blocks after the pool opens, the hook adds a swap fee in the paired currency, collected through beforeSwap/afterSwap return deltas, that starts at 30% and decays linearly to 0%. Max buy per swap at launch: for the first 60 minutes after pool initialization, a single swap cannot buy more than 1% of the total supply of the launched token: afterSwap reads the launched-token amount the swap delivers (from the BalanceDelta) and reverts if it is above the limit. launches.summary: Marginalia (x.com/marginalia_md): notes in the margin of every trade.
launches.request: Marginalia (x.com/marginalia_md): notes in the margin of every trade. Token name "Marginalia", symbol "MARG", 18 decimals, fixed supply. Callbacks: beforeInitialize, beforeSwap with beforeSwapReturnDelta, afterSwap with afterSwapReturnDelta (flags 0x20cc). Fee rule: no hook fee on buys; MARG sells pay 1% plus a 0.1 IMD stamp with a note in hookData, 3% without; exact-output quiet sells are refused (exact-input only). Where fees go: kept as IMD claims in the hook, split at accrual 70% to the week's thesis prize and 30% to the day's writer refund; never sold for ETH. Who can change it: nobody; no owner, admin, pause, upgrade or setter anywhere. Launch kind univ4_hook on Ethereum mainnet paired with IMD 0xD34a99Bc0f67aE1bbd63C660e6d0b0dd03E263B7, LP fee 12500, tick spacing 60. MarginaliaHook(IPoolManager, token, factory): validates its permissions, binds the first pool initialized through it (requires the supplied factory and fee 12500, never blocks the factory's seeding, liquidity or fee claims, refuses later pools). Its constructor clones (EIP-1167) three companions from the LIVE implementations of launch #1240 and initialises each once: MarginaliaRouter 0x365CcB3cfBC430600485234F56FD5ECb23fd70D1, MarginaliaJudge 0xC93460730a79a22282f063A0c6BA5E340Ac372b4, MarginaliaTreasury 0xe2086012f5F9CC7cAECDBC70dE392e263aAe8481; it calls the stateless MarginaliaPricer 0xEaff9B262341A0cB05579227e662BFE768A71cfb by staticcall. These addresses are compile-time constants in src/MarginaliaImpls.sol, verified by the mainnet-fork rehearsal in test/fork; the constructor reads no chain state (it must pass an empty-EVM rehearsal), and a codeless companion would revert on first use. Do not redeploy the companions. NOTES. Buying MARG through the router with a note in hookData posts a falsifiable call on any ERC-20 X priced on a canonical Uniswap v4, v3 or v2 venue: side BUY or SELL, target at least 10% away, horizon 1-90 days, text up to 280 chars in the event. Cost: a flat 0.1 IMD stamp (to the pools), a fixed 0.25 IMD spent on MARG through the pool, and an IMD bond the author sizes between 0.25 and 10 IMD by how much IMD they send, held as IMD claims for the horizon; a noted sell bonds the minimum off its IMD output. The router may trade X in the same transaction (class Traded); contract authors are class Agent. A THESIS (target 0, up to 8 KB) bonds the same way and needs a child call of the author within 7 days or forfeits. SEALED NOTES. seal(x, venue, hash) commits to a note before posting: it pays one stamp now (non-refundable), prices the venue's BUY and SELL baselines now and snapshots the author's X balance now; the note is then posted through the router no sooner than 30 minutes and no later than 6 hours after the seal, settles against the sealed baseline, and a sealed BUY call is refused if the author's X balance fell since the seal. Between seal and reveal only the author, X and venue are public. A lapsed seal keeps its stamp in the pools. COUNTERS. A thesis whose parentId is another author's open thesis is a rebuttal and competes in the same judged set; a call whose parentId is another author's open call on the same X from the opposite side is a counter-call. No deposit moves between them; each settles on its own price. PRICES. Posting needs a router-held checkpoint of the venue at least one hour old (checkpointVenue; windows expire after six hours): v3/v2 baselines are accumulator TWAPs since the checkpoint, v4 and ETH/IMD-hub baselines the window extreme adverse to the call. RESOLUTION. Permissionless observe(noteId) in a 6-hour window after the horizon records the venue accumulator or spot, the hub leg and the author's balance (bounded-gas read; a failed read counts as not held); at least 3 observations 20 blocks apart spanning at least one hour; a slot is replaced by a more adverse reading. Settle price: TWAP first-to-last on v3/v2, the observation least favourable to the call on v4 and the hub leg; fewer observations or an unpriceable series is VoidNoData (deposit back, scored as wrong). BUY calls must keep their post balance (else VoidSold); SELL calls settle on price alone. RIGHT returns exactly the bonded IMD; WRONG, VoidSold and retractions forfeit it to the pools at once. The hook never holds MARG claims and sells no pot (the deployed judge's convertForfeits finds potMarg() == 0). settle is permissionless and pays the keeper 10% of a forfeited bond. SCORE. score += difficulty x outcome (+1 right, -1 wrong, broken or unproven, -0.5 retracted), difficulty = log2(multiple) x sqrt(30/horizon) x market-cap tier, on every venue. The score is reputation only: no pool pays for it, so a self-provisioned venue (an author as its only LP and trader) can inflate a number but never draw money; every call keeps its right/wrong/broken tallies and the writer refund. PAYOUTS. Thesis prize: once a week, when the pool holds at least 2 IMD, the judge clone buys the panel's ranking of the week's theses through the IMD Intake 0x1397434cd35e8a9C8aC312A61D3A285EB31dea56 (0.5 IMD, head 3, evidence panel) and the hook pays 50/30/20; an empty eligible head rolls the pool forward. Writer refund: every non-retracted note of a day claims an equal split capped at one stamp. Unclaimed pools sweep forward after 28 days. The treasury drips 2% of its IMD into the pools daily. Build from this repository as it is: audit, adapt only what deployment strictly requires, keep all numbers and rules, deploy. Tests: forge test --no-match-path 'test/fork/*' (179 tests); the fork suite needs MAINNET_RPC_URL.

Kiln: a Uniswap v4 hook for a new ETH/ZTO pool that charges a lower fee to wallets holding Pepeolithic NFTs, keeps the fee everyone else pays as a ZTO reserve, and uses that reserve to buy Pepeolithic pieces from anyone and sell them back. Two contracts, Launcher and Kiln. Deploy on Ethereum mainnet (chain id 1). Nothing is upgradeable, pausable or ownable; no admin exists anywhere; the reserve can never be withdrawn, only paid out for pieces.

ADDRESSES (constants). ZTO 0xd782bdea4ef02a0bd391eb9089470c8080f0a68e (plain ERC-20, 18 decimals, write 18 as a constant). Pepeolithic (PEPEO, ERC-721, 737 ids) 0x765956a7307222346b08fff681820a5d77e92028. Uniswap v4 PoolManager 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90. Native ETH is currency0 (address 0), ZTO currency1.

CONSTRUCTORS take static words only (address, uint, bool, bytes32: the deployment manifest supports nothing else, no arrays, no int24), make no external calls and read nothing on-chain (the verifier deploys in an empty EVM). Launcher constructor args: zto, pepeo, poolManager (three addresses, nothing else). EVERY OTHER NUMBER IS A CODE CONSTANT: tickSpacing 60 (int24 constant), lpFee 2000 (0.20%, static pool fee), the pass tiers minPepes 0 / 1 / 3 / 7 / 12 / 21 with kilnCut 13000 / 10000 / 7500 / 5000 / 2500 / 0 in hundredths of a bip (1.30%, 1.00%, 0.75%, 0.50%, 0.25%, 0%), spreadBps 1500 (15%), depth 50. The Kiln is created by the Launcher with CREATE2 and takes (zto, pepeo, poolManager) too; it must NOT validate its own address bits in its constructor; the Launcher checks them after CREATE2. The Launcher exposes initCodeHash() (view) so the salt can be mined off-chain.

LAUNCHER. One permissionless function open(bytes32 salt, uint160 sqrtPriceX96) that succeeds once: (1) deploys the Kiln with CREATE2 and reverts unless its address carries exactly the permission bits for beforeSwap, afterSwap, beforeSwapReturnDelta and afterSwapReturnDelta and no others; (2) initializes the ETH/ZTO pool on the PoolManager with lpFee, tickSpacing and the Kiln as hook at sqrtPriceX96; emits Opened(kiln, poolId). No liquidity is added by the Launcher: the deployer adds a ZTO-only range position later through the normal PositionManager, so the Kiln must not restrict liquidity in any way (no liquidity callbacks).

KILN, FEE PASS. On every swap in its pool the Kiln reads pepes = PEPEO.balanceOf(tx.origin) (routers are msg.sender; tx.origin is the trader) and picks the highest tier whose minPepes <= pepes. The pool's static lpFee goes to liquidity as usual; on top, the Kiln takes kilnCut of the swap as its cut, ALWAYS IN ZTO: when ZTO is the input, from the input (beforeSwap return delta on the specified currency for exact-input, afterSwap on the unspecified for exact-output); when ETH is the input, from the ZTO output (afterSwap return delta for exact-input, beforeSwap for exact-output). Work out each of the four cases so the trader is charged kilnCut of the ZTO side and the pool's accounting settles. The cut is NOT taken as real tokens inside the swap (the trader's input is settled by the router only after the swap, so poolManager.take would revert on an empty manager): the hook settles its return delta by MINTING ERC-6909 claim tokens for ZTO to itself (poolManager.mint(address(this), zto, amount)) and adds the amount to `claims`. collect(): permissionless, burns the Kiln's whole ZTO claim balance and takes real ZTO out of the PoolManager (poolManager.unlock -> burn + take, or the equivalent), moving the amount from `claims` into `reserve`; sell() and buy() call collect() first. Tier 21 pays no cut at all. Emit Passed(trader, pepes, kilnCut, ztoTaken) per swap and Collected(amount) per collect(). No block-held guard; README states that a pass only needs to be in the wallet during the swap.

KILN, PIECES. State: claims (ZTO cut still held as ERC-6909 claims), reserve (real ZTO held for pieces; grows by collect(), seeds and sales of pieces; shrinks only by buying pieces; reserve <= ZTO.balanceOf(Kiln) always), inventory (ids held). Views: claims(), bid() = reserve / depth (real ZTO only, so it is always payable); ask() = bid() * (10000 + spreadBps) / 10000; inventory(), reserve(), tierOf(address), poolKey(). sell(uint256 id): the caller's PEPEO piece is pulled with transferFrom (caller approves first), price = bid() before the transfer, reserve -= price, ZTO.transfer(caller, price) requiring the bool, emits Sold(id, seller, price); reverts if bid() is 0. buy(uint256 id): id must be in inventory; price = ask(); ZTO.transferFrom(caller, kiln, price) requiring the bool, reserve += price, piece sent to caller with transferFrom (never safeTransferFrom, no receiver callbacks), emits Bought(id, buyer, price). seed(uint256 amount): anyone adds ZTO to reserve by transferFrom, emits Seeded(from, amount). No other way moves ZTO or pieces. Pieces arriving by plain transfer without sell() are not inventory and are stuck; README says so. Because bid is reserve/depth it is always payable, falls geometrically as pieces come in and rises with every cut, seed and sale.

TESTS against the real v4 PoolManager (vendor v4-core and v4-periphery test routers) with a mock ZTO and a mock ERC-721: open() once and only at an address with the right bits; a ZTO-only range position above the opening price added through the test liquidity router; swaps in all four cases (ETH in / ZTO in, exact in / exact out) for wallets holding 0, 1, 3, 7, 12 and 21 pieces, checking the ZTO cut equals kilnCut of the ZTO side within rounding, that tier 21 pays nothing, that the cut shows in claims() and after collect() in reserve() and the Kiln's real ZTO balance, that collect() with nothing to collect is a harmless no-op, and that the trader also paid lpFee; sell() pays bid and bid falls afterwards; buy() charges ask and the piece leaves inventory; buy of an id not held reverts; sell at zero reserve reverts; seed() grows bid; reserve never exceeds the Kiln's ZTO balance; nobody can withdraw. README with the rules, the tier table and the two caveats (tx.origin, stuck transfers). BUILD: solidity 0.8.26, optimizer + via-IR (via_ir = true, optimizer_runs = 1), custom errors only, no ReentrancyGuard (external token calls last), Kiln deployed code under 12,000 bytes. Slither: multiply before dividing; string.concat not encodePacked.

launches.summary: On-Chain Oppenheimer's NUKE token is launched paired with IMD on Uniswap v4 pool using a dedicated hook named NUKEHook.
launches.request:
[SIMD-LAUNCH]
Token name: On-Chain Oppenheimer
Token symbol: NUKE

On-Chain Oppenheimer's NUKE token is launched paired with IMD on Uniswap v4 pool using a dedicated hook named NUKEHook. The total fixed supply is 1,000,000,000 tokens with 18 decimals, 10% allocated off-chain to the swarm, and 90% supplied directly to the pool at launch. The token itself is a standard ERC-20 with no custom logic or fees. 

CONTRACT: NUKEHook (the launch pool's hook)
1. Immutable constants: 1% hook fee (100 bps) taken afterSwap on the actual BalanceDelta of the unspecified currency (could be launched token or IMD), matching the exact amount filled for fairness.
2.

Mechanics specification (authoritative: where anything above differs, follow these exactly):
M1. Buyback and burn in batches: on EVERY swap (buys and sells) the hook takes an extra 1% in afterSwap from the actual BalanceDelta, on the unspecified currency (afterSwapReturnDelta), so the fee always matches what filled. On a buy that currency is usually the launched token; on a sell it is usually the paired currency. Launched-token fees are burned: an anyone-callable sweep() sends them to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD. Paired-currency fees accrue in the hook to fund buybacks and are never spent inside a swap callback. executeBatch(), callable by anyone in its own transaction, runs at most once every 3600 seconds; its budget is up to 25% of the accrued paired-currency balance, and it swaps exact-input through the PoolManager (unlock and swap) with a sqrtPriceLimit 300 bps beyond a time-weighted reference price kept by the hook, accepting a partial fill: whatever does not fit inside that limit stays accrued for the next batch, so the buyback can never deadlock. The price limit is the only slippage guard (no minimum-output check that hardcodes the LP fee). Batch swaps are made by the hook itself and pay no hook fee. Bought tokens go to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD. Immutable constants; views pending(), pendingBurn(), lastBatch(), referencePrice().

Build requirements (mandatory):
- A complete Foundry project at the repository root: foundry.toml with solc 0.8.26, evm_version cancun, optimizer on and bytecode_hash = "none", so the build is reproducible and every deployed contract can be source-verified (Sourcify/Etherscan) right after deploy: every contract the deployer deploys lives in src/, and every import resolves to a file committed in the repo (lib/ vendored, remappings.txt).
- Contracts: NUKEHook. The hook is the hook of this launch's pool; keep its creation code within the EIP-3860 size limit.
- No selfdestruct and no delegatecall anywhere in runtime code. No proxies, no owner, no upgradeability.
- Chain: Ethereum mainnet (chainId 1). Uniswap v4 PoolManager: 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90 (pass it to the hook constructor).
- Paired currency: IMD, the ERC-20 at 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7 on Ethereum mainnet (18 decimals).
- Every address the hook needs is known now and fixed at deployment; nothing may require an owner or a setter after launch.
- Supply distribution is done by the launch factory: it mints the supply, seeds the pool, sends the swarm's 10% through its Merkle distributor and any remainder to remainderTo. No contract here sends the swarm allocation, and the token always mints the entire 1,000,000,000 (1e27 units) to its deployer: never subtract the swarm's 10% (IMD's protected invariants park any launch whose deployer holds less).
- Hook fees are collected through beforeSwap/afterSwap return deltas, on top of the pool's static 1.25% LP fee (fee tier 12500). Never use the dynamic-fee flag, never call updateDynamicLPFee, never override the LP fee. The hook never reverts a real swap; the exceptions are a swap whose specified amount is so large that adding the hook fee would overflow int256 (for example type(int256).max requests): it may revert with UnrepresentableFee. That is the accepted swap domain.
- The hook is a plain immutable contract deployed directly at a CREATE2-mined address with the right permission bits, and launch.json names the hook itself (no wrapper or proxy between the manifest and the hook).
- Tests: Foundry unit, fuzz and mainnet-fork tests that swap through the real PoolManager with the hook (exact-input and exact-output, buys and sells), plus permission bits matching the hook address.
- Every hook fee is proportional to what actually filled. Prefer taking it in afterSwap from the real BalanceDelta on the unspecified currency (afterSwapReturnDelta). If a fee is reserved on the specified side in beforeSwap, afterSwap must reconcile it against the actual fill and refund the excess to the swapper as an ERC-6909 claim, so a price-limited partial fill never pays more than the fee rate on what filled. Test exact-input and exact-output partial fills with a price limit.
- launch.json pool: pairedCurrency 0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7, fee 12500, tickSpacing 60, initialPrice "79228162514264337593543950336" (provenance only; the launch factory sets the opening price from the economics). Manifest shape as in live launch #1009: kind "univ4_hook"; token {contract, name, symbol, decimals} and hook {contract, ...} where each contract is a bare Solidity contract name like "NUKE" or "NUKEHook" (never a path or "File.sol:Name"); hook {contract, constructorArgs (e.g. ["$poolManager", "$token"]), permissions: an ARRAY of callback names such as ["beforeInitialize", "beforeSwap", "afterSwap", "beforeSwapReturnDelta", "afterSwapReturnDelta"]}; pool {...}; notes: a string explaining constructor args, permission bits and fees.

launches.summary: When the hook acts: after every swap (afterSwap), plus once at pool initialization (beforeInitialize) to lock the hook to this launch's pool.
launches.request:
When the hook acts: after every swap (afterSwap), plus once at pool initialization (beforeInitialize) to lock the hook to this launch's pool.
Fee rule: the hook takes no fee. No fees, only the launchpad's standard trading fee (LP fee 12500, 1.25%).
Where fees go: nowhere; the hook never takes or moves any funds.
Who can change it: nobody. No owner, no admin, no upgrades, no settings.
Token name: Pixel Pool
Token symbol: PIXEL

Build PIXEL POOL on Ethereum mainnet, kind univ4_hook, paired with IMD (0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7): the launch token and its Uniswap v4 pool with our hook, which paints a 32x32 dot canvas on chain, one dot per swap.

TOKEN PixelToken (src/PixelToken.sol): plain ERC20, name "Pixel Pool", symbol "PIXEL", 18 decimals, no constructor arguments, fixed supply 10^27 units minted once to its deployer, ordinary transfers, no mint, tax, owner or proxy.

HOOK PixelPoolHook (src/PixelPoolHook.sol, Solidity 0.8.26, Foundry, depends only on v4-core):
1. Implements IHooks directly. Constructor(IPoolManager manager, address token) in that order; validates permissions with Hooks.validateHookPermissions. Permissions: beforeInitialize and afterSwap only (address mask 0x2040). No return deltas, never touches funds.
2. beforeInitialize: only the PoolManager, only once, only for the pool of this hook with the launch token and IMD; stores poolId and quoteIsCurrency0 (true when currency0 is not the launch token). Any later initialize reverts. Every enabled callback reverts unless msg.sender is the PoolManager; afterSwap reverts for any other pool.
3. afterSwap paints one dot: strokes += 1; pixel = (strokes - 1) % 1024. Dots fill in order, left to right, top to bottom; after 1024 swaps a new pass repaints from the top left.
4. Color: BUY = IMD in, PIXEL out (buy = zeroForOne == quoteIsCurrency0) is GREEN; SELL is RED. Shade by the absolute IMD amount of the swap delta: < 5, < 50, < 500, >= 500 IMD (18 decimals) -> index 0..3. Palette index: 0 empty, 1..4 green #1f7a3d #22b455 #2ee66b #8dffad, 5..8 red #7a1f1f #c42b2b #ff3b3b #ff9a9a, empty #0b0b12.
5. Storage: 1024 one-byte palette indexes packed 32 per slot in uint256[32], leftmost dot in the least significant byte of each row.
6. Event Painted(uint256 indexed stroke, uint256 indexed pixel, uint8 color, address indexed painter) with painter = tx.origin.
7. Views: strokes(), pixelAt(i), canvas() returning uint256[32], quoteIsCurrency0(), render() returning an SVG of the dots built in a preallocated buffer, under 15M gas on a full canvas.
8. No owner, admin, upgrade, pause or post deploy calls. Keep it small; no features beyond this spec.

TESTS (Foundry, against a real v4 PoolManager): dots paint in order; buy green and sell red with IMD as currency0 AND as currency1; bigger swaps brighter; second pass repaints; only one pool; only PoolManager; render under the gas limit.

Launch manifest: launch.json must be exactly this JSON:
{
  "kind": "univ4_hook",
  "hook": {
    "contract": "PixelPoolHook",
    "constructorArgs": ["$poolManager", "$token"],
    "permissions": ["beforeInitialize", "afterSwap"]
  },
  "token": { "contract": "PixelToken", "name": "Pixel Pool", "symbol": "PIXEL", "decimals": 18 },
  "pool": {
    "pairedCurrency": "0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7",
    "fee": 12500,
    "tickSpacing": 60,
    "initialPrice": "79228162514264337593543950336"
  },
  "notes": "PIXEL POOL on Ethereum mainnet paired with IMD. launches.request:
When the hook acts: after every swap (afterSwap), plus once at pool initialization (beforeInitialize) to lock the hook to this launch's pool.
Fee rule: the hook takes no fee. No fees, only the launchpad's standard trading fee.
Where fees go: nowhere; the hook never takes or moves any funds.
Who can change it: nobody. No owner, no admin, no upgrades, no settings.
Token name: Pixel Pool
Token symbol: PIXEL

Build PIXEL POOL: a Uniswap v4 hook whose pool paints a 32x32 dot canvas, one dot per swap, fully on chain. The pool pairs the new token with IMD (0xD34a99Bc0f67aE1bbd63C660e6d0b0dd03E263B7).

CONTRACT PixelPoolHook (Solidity 0.8.26, Foundry, depends only on v4-core):
1. Implements IHooks directly (no BaseHook). Permissions: beforeInitialize and afterSwap only. No return deltas, never touches funds. Constructor takes only the PoolManager and validates permissions.
2. beforeInitialize: the first pool initialized with the hook is stored as its only pool (poolId). Any later initialize reverts PoolAlreadySet. Every hook entry reverts NotPoolManager unless msg.sender is the PoolManager. afterSwap reverts WrongPool for any other pool.
3. beforeInitialize also stores which side is the quote currency: quoteIsCurrency0 = (currency0 is IMD or native ETH). The other side is the launch token. This makes buy and sell correct whatever the address order is.
4. afterSwap paints one dot: strokes += 1; pixel = (strokes - 1) % 1024. Dots fill in order, left to right, top to bottom; after 1024 swaps a new pass starts at the top left and repaints over the old dots.
5. Color: a BUY is a swap where the quote currency goes in and the launch token comes out (buy = zeroForOne == quoteIsCurrency0). BUY is GREEN, SELL is RED. Shade by the absolute quote side amount of the swap delta: < 5 IMD, < 50 IMD, < 500 IMD, >= 500 IMD (in 18 decimals) -> index 0..3. Palette index: 0 empty, 1..4 green, 5..8 red. Hex: 1 #1f7a3d, 2 #22b455, 3 #2ee66b, 4 #8dffad, 5 #7a1f1f, 6 #c42b2b, 7 #ff3b3b, 8 #ff9a9a, empty #0b0b12.
6. Storage: 1024 one-byte palette indexes packed 32 per slot in uint256[32].
7. Event Painted(uint256 indexed stroke, uint256 indexed pixel, uint8 color, address indexed painter) with painter = tx.origin.
8. Views: strokes(), pass() (1 + (strokes-1)/1024, 1 when empty), pixelAt(i), canvas() returning 1024 bytes, palette(i) returning bytes7 hex, quoteIsCurrency0(), render() returning an SVG (viewBox 0 0 32 36, dark background, one path per color, each dot a 0.8 square offset 0.1 so dots show gaps, footer text "PIXEL POOL  pass N  swaps M"), renderURI() returning data:image/svg+xml;base64. render must build into a preallocated buffer (no repeated abi.encodePacked concatenation) and stay under 15M gas on a full canvas.
9. No owner, no admin, no upgrade, no post deploy calls. Keep it small and readable; no features beyond this spec.

TESTS (Foundry, against a real v4 PoolManager): swaps paint dots in order with no gaps; a buy is green and a sell red with the quote currency as currency0 AND as currency1; bigger swaps brighter; second pass repaints dots 0 and 1; only one pool; only PoolManager can call the hook; render under the gas limit on a full canvas.

kind = "univ4_hook". pool.tickSpacing = 60.
Address order is fixed on purpose: the PIXEL token MUST be deployed at an address numerically greater than IMD (0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7). Choose or mine the token's CREATE2 salt so this holds, and add a test that asserts PIXEL > IMD for the planned deployment. So currency0 = IMD and currency1 = PIXEL.
Opening price: 2,500 IMD market cap for 1,000,000,000 PIXEL = 400,000 PIXEL per IMD (both 18 decimals). pool.initialPrice = "50108289675009586237282760313921" (decimal string, sqrtPriceX96 of currency1/currency0). If the launch factory sets these itself, use the factory values.

launches.request:
Build a token with a Uniswap v4 hook and an NFT reward distributor for the Swarm Pepe collection (SPEPE, 0x999ce0CE8C5f7661e0c74a568FfE27CEB9177bDB, Ethereum mainnet). The collection contract cannot be changed and has no transfer hooks. Minting is still open (verify onchain; totalSupply() reverts, use totalMinted()). Launch kind univ4_hook on Ethereum mainnet, paired with ETH: the launch's standard token and pool with our hook, plus our distributor and auction contracts. Deploy in the launch. No website in this job: an existing site will integrate the contracts later, so keep clean ABIs, events and the views below. No owner powers after launch, no upgradeability, no pause.

Token name: OG. Symbol: OG. The launch's standard token (1,000,000,000, 18 decimals, plain transfers); "burn" in this spec means sending to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD, counted in a public totalBurned.

START FROM EXISTING CODE: this exact project was already built and accepted (build_contract_project, all checks passed) in job a38b37bd-6caa-4756-9aa2-6033c44ac713; its source is the accepted bundle https://api.imd.fun/bundles/8d918c729607f1be5c14bc1b4d2e4b162b6f121f8462e77dad3af25760b1d064. Download it and use it as the starting point; keep its logic and only fix what review finds. That job stopped at manifest only because the pool start price was missing.

Pool (launch.json): Ethereum univ4_hook policy 34, paired with native ETH (currency0 = ETH, currency1 = OG), fee 12500, tickSpacing 60, opening market cap 10 ETH per policy (100,000,000 OG per ETH), initialPrice 792281625142643375935439503360000 (decimal sqrtPriceX96).

When the hook acts: on every swap in this pool, taking its fee from the settled ETH deltas (beforeSwap/afterSwap with return deltas), and enforcing the launch protection below.

HOOK FEE: 3.5% on every buy and every sell, always taken in ETH (from the ETH input on buys, from the ETH output on sells), computed on actual settled deltas for exact-input and exact-output swaps. Of it: 2.5% of the trade to the distributor, 1% of the trade to the team wallet 0x90738ABe9b04622Dc0b3d015a3964Cc7D1Fd1859.

LAUNCH PROTECTION: open to everyone from the first block. For the first 60 minutes after the pool opens, the buy fee decays linearly from 50% to the normal 3.5%. Everything above 3.5% goes to the distributor backlog, none to the team. After minute 60: normal fees.

DISTRIBUTOR (per tokenId, weighted, no loops):
- An NFT earns nothing until activated. Levels and weights: L1 = 1, L2 = 2, L3 = 4.
- Activation burns OG. Cumulative cost: L1 = 50,000, L2 = 150,000, L3 = 400,000 OG (upgrading pays only the difference). Costs fixed in code, no oracle. Only the current ownerOf(tokenId) can activate or upgrade. Also activation with ETH: the contract buys the exact OG amount through the pool (paying the hook fee like any buyer) and burns it.
- Accrual: accPerWeight += eth * SCALE / totalWeight; pending(id) = weight[id] * accPerWeight / SCALE - debt[id]. A new activation or upgrade settles pending first and sets debt at the current accumulator, so it never earns past fees.
- Level and pending ETH belong to the tokenId and travel with the NFT on any transfer or marketplace sale.
- Backlog: fees that arrive while totalWeight = 0 (and the launch-protection surplus) are held and streamed into the accumulator linearly over 30 days once something is active, never paid as a windfall to the first activator.

EXIT (the only way to get ETH):
- No claim that keeps the NFT. To receive its pending ETH, the owner hands the NFT to the contract and is paid everything accrued on it in the same transaction. Its level is cleared and its weight leaves totalWeight.
- Exit is not allowed within 24 hours after the NFT's last activation or upgrade.

AUCTION:
- The exited NFT is immediately listed in a Dutch auction priced in OG.
- Start price = max(10x the previous auction's sale price, 500,000 OG). Exponential decay over 36 hours down to a floor of 50,000 OG; at the floor it stays listed until someone buys.
- 100% of auction proceeds are burned. The buyer receives the NFT at level 0 with zero accrual and must activate it to earn.

VIEWS for the existing website (also emit an event for every activation, upgrade, exit, auction listing, sale and fee split): totalWeight, active NFTs per level, pending(id), level(id), backlog left and its stream end, current auctions with live prices, last sale price, total burned, launch fee now and minutes left of the decay.

TESTS (Foundry, mainnet fork): fee in ETH on both sides and both exact modes and the 2.5/1 split; launch fee decay over 60 minutes and surplus to backlog; weighted accrual and upgrade math; no retroactive rewards; backlog streaming with zero active; level and pending travelling with transfers; exit payout and the 24h lock; auction start/decay/floor and burn; reentrancy on ETH sends and ERC-721 transfers; ETH solvency and weight conservation invariants. Independent review of the economics and every contract.
